postmortem.summary: Two incidents touched quote drafting after launch. To stop the first, long drafts were sent to a larger model, and that routing stayed in place. It is the main driver of the cost running over the brief's budget in early November. Prices stayed in fixed code throughout, as the brief's line says.

what_went_well: The line held: the model drafts the text and fixed code sets every price.
The timeouts were stopped the same afternoon they were reported.

fixes.fix: Send only drafts over the standard model's context limit to vendor-a/xl, and route the rest back.
fixes.done_when: cost-budget-check reads tokens per task within budget for a full two-week window.

fixes.fix: Give every routing change made during an incident an end date, and list the open ones in the weekly incident review.
fixes.done_when: The incident template has an end-date field, and the weekly review shows the open list.

fixes.fix: Put the cost-budget-check result beside the eval-kit result on every quote drafting release candidate.
fixes.done_when: The next release candidate's checklist links both, and a build over budget is held for a decision.

fixes.fix: Show 'price updating' and retry when the price book sync lags, instead of price pending.
fixes.done_when: A staged sync delay shows the message, and the draft fills in when the sync completes.

questions.question: What did we bet on, and how will we know it worked?
questions.answer: Tradespeople spend evenings writing quotes by hand, so quotes go out late and lose the job. The bar: Quote draft acceptance rate at 40% or higher by 2026-11-15 [F01]. Head of Product, Quoting squad decides the next step.

questions.question: Did it land?
questions.answer: did-it-land says landed. Quote draft acceptance rate reads 43% [F02] to 2026-11-23, against a bar of 40% [F03] by 2026-11-15. At the date it read 41% [F04]. Flags on the read: over-cost-budget.
asked_last_time: Are customers actually using the quote drafts?

questions.question: Is the move real, or normal noise?
questions.answer: Before launch the metric averaged 21.7% [F05], with a spread of 3.83% [F06]. By the date it sat 5.05 spreads above that mean [F07]. That rules out noise. It does not say what moved it: no holdout group is in the record.

questions.question: Did the result the metric should move, move too?
questions.answer: The outcome series (Illustrative CRM export, quotes_won_weekly.csv) went from 31 [F08] on 2026-08-31 to 36 [F09] on 2026-11-23. It moved the same way as the metric; the record does not show why.

questions.question: What did we decide, and who decided?
questions.answer: From decision-record, as of 2026-11-26: 5 decided [F10]. Set the rollback trigger for quote drafting (Head of Product, Quoting squad, 2026-08-10); Choose the model tier for quote drafts (Tech lead, Quoting squad, 2026-08-10); Build quote drafting now, against its landing brief (Head of Product, Quoting squad, 2026-07-27).

questions.question: Is quality holding as more of the work runs without a person?
questions.answer: v1.4's held-out pass rate is 80% [F11] on 30 cases [F13] (95% interval 62.7% to 90.5%). 71.5% of tasks finished with no person [F12]. eval-kit's build check: not confirmed: inside noise. The point estimate meets the target, but the low end of the 95% interval does not clear it.

questions.question: Is v1.4 really better than v1.3?
questions.answer: Held-out pass rate went from 70% [F14] on v1.3 to 80% [F11] on v1.4, on the same cases. eval-kit marks the gain as inside the noise for this case count, so it is not yet a proven gain.

questions.question: What does each task cost, against the budget?
questions.answer: $0.0338 per task [F15] from 2026-11-01 to 2026-11-14, against a budget of $0.027 [F16]: over budget by 25% [F17]. Tokens per task: 10,300 [F18] against 9,000 [F19]. Price per token: $0.00000328 [F20] against $0.000003 [F21]. cost-budget-check computes these; eval-kit cites the same cost per task.
asked_last_time: What does the AI cost us per quote?

questions.question: Who brings cost back within budget, and by when?
questions.answer: The record names the model behind most of it, vendor-a/xl: $0.963 [F22] of $1.89 [F23] over budget. The postmortem names the fix: Send only drafts over the standard model's context limit to vendor-a/xl, and route the rest back. Owner: Lead, Quoting squad, due 2026-12-10.

questions.question: Was it ready to ship when it shipped?
questions.answer: release-readiness said ready to ship for Acme quote drafting v1.0 on 2026-09-05: 6 [F24] of 7 [F25] checks ready to ship. Open bugs within the severity limits read hold under a waiver from Head of Product, Quoting squad until 2026-09-19. Every spec-auditor hold was closed before release (rollback, eval-plan).

questions.question: Was the waived check closed before its waiver ran out?
questions.missing: Open bugs within the severity limits: waived by Head of Product, Quoting squad until 2026-09-19. No later release check in the record says it closed.

questions.question: What are customers saying about it?
questions.answer: customer-signal-digest says problem still raised. It read 21 signals [F26] from 16 accounts [F27] from 2026-09-07 to 2026-11-24. 7 signals [F28] from 7 accounts [F29] say the problem is still there. The top problem theme: Quote drafts miss line items.

questions.question: What went wrong, and who owns each fix?
questions.answer: The learning review of 2026-11-26 covers 2 incidents [F30] from 2026-09-07 to 2026-11-26. Each change it lists cites its evidence. 4 fixes [F31], each with one owner and a due date: Send only drafts over the standard model's context limit to vendor-a/xl, and route the rest back (Lead, Quoting squad, due 2026-12-10); Give every routing change made during an incident an end date, and list the open ones in the weekly incident review (Product manager, Quoting squad, due 2026-12-17); Put the cost-budget-check result beside the eval-kit result on every quote drafting release candidate (Tech lead, Quoting squad, due 2027-01-08); Show 'price updating' and retry when the price book sync lags, instead of price pending (Product manager, Quoting squad, due 2026-12-17).

questions.question: Why this bet, over the others?
questions.answer: bet-portfolio-review ranked it 4 of 8 bets, 1 needs work first [F32] on 2026-07-27. Its brief scored 14 points of 14 [F33].
